title: Third stage of labor: placenta separation and delivery
description: Study uterine contraction, maternal placental bed, cord, membranes, placenta delivery and postpartum bleeding anatomy.

questions.question: When does the third stage of labor begin and end?
questions.answer: It begins after the baby is born and ends when the placenta and fetal membranes are delivered. Postpartum monitoring continues after that stage.

questions.question: Why does the uterus contract after the baby is born?
questions.answer: Uterine contraction shrinks the placental attachment area, supports separation and compresses maternal blood vessels to limit bleeding. Actual uterine tone must be assessed clinically.

questions.question: Which surfaces does a delivered placenta have?
questions.answer: A fetal-facing surface is covered by amnion and joined to the cord, while a maternal-facing surface reflects its attachment to uterine decidual tissue. Examination of a delivered placenta is a clinical task.

questions.question: What do the three placenta-related images in this chapter show?
questions.answer: The new third-stage digital image models an empty uterus after birth with a partly separating placenta, not a completed placental delivery. A second image depicts an attached placenta during pregnancy, and a third digital microscopic-scale cutaway shows a chorionic villus before delivery. None is a real patient photograph.

questions.question: Is heavy bleeding after birth a normal event to assess from art?
questions.answer: No. Heavy postpartum bleeding can be an emergency needing urgent professional evaluation. The image cannot measure blood loss, diagnose retained placenta or guide treatment.
